plugins.name: ASUS Router / ZenWiFi
plugins.description: ASUS ASUSWRT — client list with hostnames, WAN status, bandwidth
plugins.credentials_hint: Your ASUS router admin username and password
plugins.ai_prompt:
Write a NetSentinel hardware plugin for my ASUS router at {ip}. Install 'pip install asusrouter' first.

The plugin must export:
  HARDWARE_NAME = 'ASUS Router'
  HARDWARE_TYPE = 'router'
  HARDWARE_IP = '{ip}'
  def get_info() -> dict
  def get_status() -> dict  (include connected_clients count, mesh_nodes count)
  def get_clients() -> list  (each item: ip, mac, hostname, band, unit)

Use the asusrouter library: AsusRouter class, method async_get_connected_devices(). Since it's async, wrap with asyncio.run(). Map device fields: ip, mac, name→hostname, connection_type→band.

plugins.name: AVM FRITZ!Box
plugins.description: FRITZ!Box via TR-064 — client list, WAN IP, DSL sync stats, uptime
plugins.credentials_hint: Your FRITZ!Box admin password (shown on the label on the device)
plugins.ai_prompt:
Write a NetSentinel hardware plugin for my AVM FRITZ!Box at {ip}. Install 'pip install fritzconnection' first.

The plugin must export:
  HARDWARE_NAME = 'AVM FRITZ!Box'
  HARDWARE_TYPE = 'router'
  HARDWARE_IP = '{ip}'
  def get_info() -> dict
  def get_status() -> dict  (wan_ip, uptime_sec, connected_clients count)
  def get_clients() -> list  (each: ip, mac, hostname, band)

Use FritzHosts(address=HARDWARE_IP, password=pw) to get active_hosts(). Use FritzStatus for WAN IP and uptime. No username needed, only password.

plugins.name: Ubiquiti UniFi
plugins.description: UniFi controller — full client list with SSID, band, signal, hostname
plugins.credentials_hint: Your UniFi Network admin username and password
plugins.ai_prompt:
Write a NetSentinel hardware plugin for my Ubiquiti UniFi controller at {ip}. Install 'pip install pyunifi' first.

The plugin must export:
  HARDWARE_NAME = 'Ubiquiti UniFi'
  HARDWARE_TYPE = 'router'
  HARDWARE_IP = '{ip}'
  def get_info() -> dict
  def get_status() -> dict  (connected_clients count)
  def get_clients() -> list  (each: ip, mac, hostname, band, unit=ap_mac)

Use Controller(host, username, password, version='UDMP-unifiOS', ssl_verify=False) from pyunifi.controller. Call get_clients(). Map: ip, mac, hostname, radio→band ('ng'→'2.4G' '5G-1'→'5G'), ap_mac→unit.

plugins.name: Netgear Router / Orbi
plugins.description: Netgear router — connected devices with IP, MAC, hostname, connection type
plugins.ai_prompt:
Write a NetSentinel hardware plugin for my Netgear router at {ip}. Install 'pip install pynetgear' first.

The plugin must export:
  HARDWARE_NAME = 'Netgear Router'
  HARDWARE_TYPE = 'router'
  HARDWARE_IP = '{ip}'
  def get_info() -> dict
  def get_status() -> dict  (connected_clients count, wan_ip)
  def get_clients() -> list  (each: ip, mac, hostname, band)

Use Netgear(password=pw, host=HARDWARE_IP) from pynetgear. Call get_attached_devices_v2(). Map: ip, mac, name→hostname, connection_type→band.

plugins.name: OpenWrt
plugins.description: OpenWrt via LUCI RPC — client list with IP, MAC, hostname, wireless band
plugins.ai_prompt:
Write a NetSentinel hardware plugin for my OpenWrt router at {ip}. Install 'pip install openwrt-luci-rpc' first.

The plugin must export:
  HARDWARE_NAME = 'OpenWrt Router'
  HARDWARE_TYPE = 'router'
  HARDWARE_IP = '{ip}'
  def get_info() -> dict
  def get_status() -> dict  (connected_clients count, wan_ip)
  def get_clients() -> list  (each: ip, mac, hostname, band)

Use OpenWrtRpc(HARDWARE_IP, 'root', password) from openwrt_luci_rpc. Call rpc.get_arp_table() and rpc.get_wireless_devices() for client data.

plugins.name: MikroTik RouterOS
plugins.description: MikroTik RouterOS via API — ARP table, DHCP leases, wireless clients
plugins.ai_prompt:
Write a NetSentinel hardware plugin for my MikroTik router at {ip}. Install 'pip install routeros-api' first.

The plugin must export:
  HARDWARE_NAME = 'MikroTik Router'
  HARDWARE_TYPE = 'router'
  HARDWARE_IP = '{ip}'
  def get_info() -> dict
  def get_status() -> dict  (connected_clients, wan_ip)
  def get_clients() -> list  (each: ip, mac, hostname, band)

Use routeros_api.connect(host, username, password) on port 8728. Run commands '/ip/arp/print' and '/ip/dhcp-server/lease/print' for clients. Run '/ip/address/print' for WAN IP.

Write a NetSentinel hardware plugin for my Synology router at {ip}. Install 'pip install python-synology' first.

The plugin must export:
